title: Cherry Crumb Pie (Canned Cherries)
source: Feast and Farm and Oregon Fruit (filling), Smitten Kitchen (crumb), Stella Parks (crust), adapted

items.body: Make one shell on the Flaky Pie Dough card: rolled, chilled at least 2 h and blind-baked. It can be baked up to 12 h ahead.
In a bowl, whisk the brown sugar and granulated sugar into the melted butter until smooth.
Stir the flour and salt into the butter mixture until no dry flour shows. Press it into the bowl and cool until firm, 10–15 min.
Break it into ½–¾ in chunks, leaving some smaller. Bigger chunks stay soft in the middle. Spread on a plate or quarter sheet pan and refrigerate at least 30 min.
Open the cans and pour them into the strainer set over a bowl. Measure out 240 g (1 cup) of the liquid and pour off the rest. Leave the cherries in the strainer.

In the saucepan, whisk the sugar, cornstarch and salt, then whisk in the 240 g of cherry liquid. Bring to a boil over medium-high, stirring. Turn to medium and simmer, stirring, until thick and glossy and it coats a spoon, 3–5 min.
Off the heat, stir in the almond extract, then gently fold in the drained cherries.
Rack in the lower-middle, oven to 350 °F (177 °C). Set the cooled shell on the half sheet pan. Scrape in all the filling and spread it level.
Scatter all the cold crumb chunks over the filling without pressing them in. Leave a few small gaps so you can see the juice. Cover the crust rim with strips of foil so it doesn’t burn.
Bake until the crumb is deep golden and the filling bubbles thickly in the gaps at the center, not only at the edge, ≈45–60 min. Crumb browning too fast? Lay foil loosely on top.
Cool on a rack at least 3 h so the filling sets before slicing.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: Branded Foods labels (Meijer red tart pitted cherries in water, 15 oz, FDC 2638597; King Arthur All-Purpose; Morton; almond extract counted as Morton Bassett) and SR Legacy (sugar, brown sugar, unsalted butter, cornstarch). The cans are counted whole, liquid and all, so pouring some off makes it a little high. Shell from its card.
notes: Filling from Feast and Farm’s canned tart cherry pie (1 cup liquid, 1 cup sugar, ¼ cup cornstarch), made with 3 cans for a deeper pie; Oregon Fruit’s recipe uses the same stovetop method. Its 2 tbsp butter is left out, since the crumb has plenty. Crumb from the Dutch Apple Crumb Pie card.
Bake time is an estimate: a smaller crumb takes 40–50 min at 350 °F (177 °C), and this one is bigger. Go by the color and the bubbling.
Keeps 2 days at room temp, loosely covered; the fridge softens the crumb. To recrisp, 300 °F (149 °C) for 15–20 min, not the microwave.
